caption:
Uncle Quinn did school drop-off, lifted his nephew's very heavy bag and started to worry about little spines.

Kay's take: research hasn't clearly shown heavy bags cause kids' back pain. Sleep, screens, activity and mood seem to matter more.

What can help: two wide padded straps worn snug, heaviest items close to the back, packing only today's books, avoiding one-shoulder carrying on long walks, and looking at sleep, screens and active play. The 10% rule is a rough guide, not a firm injury line.

Get it checked if there's night pain, fever or weight loss, back pain in a child under about 10, long morning stiffness, leg weakness or numbness, or pain getting worse over weeks.
